title: Tax and Superannuation Laws Amendment (2015 Measures No. 6) Bill 2015
short_title: Tax and Superannuation Laws Amendment (2015 Measures No. 6) Bill 2015

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would change how capital gains tax applies when businesses are sold with earnout arrangements, which are rights to future payments based on the asset's performance after sale.
It would ignore capital gains and losses from these arrangements, and instead treat the payments as adjustments to the sale price, affecting the proceeds and cost of the underlying asset.
The changes apply to deals made from 17 October 2007, but are optional and beneficial, so no taxpayer would be worse off due to the retrospective effect.
changes: Disregard capital gains and losses from look-through earnout arrangements.
Treat earnout payments as adjustments to the proceeds and cost base of the underlying assets.
Apply the changes retrospectively to transactions from 17 October 2007.
summary.affected: Businesses and taxpayers involved in the sale and purchase of businesses with earnout arrangements.

speeches.speaker: Bert van Manen
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Tax and Superannuation Laws Amendment (2015 Measures No. 6) Bill 2015, which clarifies capital gains tax treatment for earn-out arrangements and introduces a 10% withholding requirement on foreign residents selling Australian real property. The speaker also noted that the top 10% of income earners pay approximately 50% of all income tax.

speeches.speaker: Tony Zappia
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the bill's two capital gains tax measures—one affecting liability and another requiring a 10% withholding on property sales by foreign residents—while criticising the coalition government for large budget deficits, $80 billion in health and education cuts, and failing to address corporate tax avoidance, noting that 38% of Australia’s largest companies paid no tax in 2013-14.

speeches.speaker: Alex Hawke
speeches.brief: The bill amends capital gains tax rules for earn-out arrangements, effective from 23 April 2015, and introduces a 10% withholding tax on foreign residents disposing of Australian property valued over $2 million from 1 July 2016.
